title: The Night Bus to Badulla: Its Silent, Extra Passenger
description:
The Kandy-Badulla night bus, a route long familiar to weary travelers, holds a darker secret in Sri Lankan folklore. Drivers whisper of a silent, sorrowful figure that appears in the deepest hours, an uninvited passenger who brings an unsettling chill and a touch of misfortune.

Join us as we recount the chilling experience of Ranga, a young conductor on his first night run, who comes face-to-face with this enduring urban legend. What happens when you encounter the silent passenger, and what price do you pay for acknowledging its presence?
fiction_note: Based on a Sri Lankan urban legend; characters and events are dramatised.

scenes.narration: The Kandy-Badulla night bus, they say, carries more than just weary travellers. Sometimes, in the deepest hours, along those winding mountain roads, it carries an extra passenger. Young Ranga, barely a month into his conductor duties, sat slumped on the folded seat near the door, the rhythm of the old bus a lullaby against the gathering rain. Beside him, Soma Aiya, the driver, gripped the wheel, his eyes fixed on the ribbon of asphalt ahead. It was Ranga’s first Badulla night run. He'd heard the stories, of course, from the older hands at the bus stand, whispers about a figure that appeared, silent and sorrowful, always at the back. He’d dismissed them, of course. Just old wives' tales, he thought, to spook the new recruits. But the air already felt heavy tonight, even before the real climb began.
visuals: Wide shot from inside a dimly lit, old Kandy-Badulla night bus, looking towards the front. Rain streaks on the windshield, blurred mountain road lights visible beyond Soma Aiya driving, Ranga slumped on his seat. Kerosene lamp glow in foreground. 35mm film.

Detail shot of Ranga's back, a young conductor in a faded uniform, sitting near the bus door. The bus interior is dark, with rain just beginning to streak the window beside him. Wet red earth road visible outside through the window, shallow depth of field, 50mm lens.

scenes.narration: Soma Aiya, without turning, grunted. 'Keep an eye on the back, putha,' he said, his voice a low rumble over the engine's drone. 'Especially on this route. Don’t want any trouble.' Ranga scoffed, adjusting his money bag. 'Trouble? Just a few sleepy villagers, Aiya. Who’d cause trouble at this hour?' Soma Aiya just hummed, a sound that seemed to carry the weight of countless midnight journeys. 'Some presences, putha, don't need to speak to cause trouble. Just to be seen. Or acknowledged.' Ranga peered back. Only a few passengers remained, scattered like forgotten parcels in the dim glow of the single fluorescent tube. He saw only shadows, and the occasional glint of a weary eye. The road was slick now, the first proper drops of rain splattering against the windshield.
visuals: Wide shot from the front of the bus, looking down the aisle. Soma Aiya's hands on the steering wheel in the foreground. Ranga, slightly blurred, turns his head to look towards the back of the bus, which is mostly dark and empty save for a few distant, indistinct shapes. Rain streaks the side windows. 35mm film.

Detail shot from Ranga's perspective, looking down the aisle. The back of the bus is a play of deep shadows and dim, distant light, with rows of empty seats. Rain streaks heavily on the windows at the very back. Telephoto lens, shallow depth of field.

scenes.narration: The bus groaned, climbing higher into the hills, the air growing colder with each winding turn. Outside, the rain intensified, a relentless drumming against the roof and streaking across the windows like tears. The towering jak trees along the roadside dissolved into blurry, dark shapes. Ranga leaned out the open door for a moment, letting the cool, damp air hit his face. The familiar smell of rain on hot earth, usually so comforting, felt different tonight, sharper, almost metallic. Far below, the scattered lights of remote villages vanished, swallowed by the dark. They were truly alone now, just the bus, its few passengers, and the endless, twisting road. And the sound of geckos, distant but persistent, seemed to call from the very fabric of the darkness itself.
visuals: Wide shot from outside the bus, a Kandy-Badulla night bus, seen from a distance on a winding mountain road. Heavy rain blurs the scene, only the bus's dim interior lights and headlights cut through the downpour. Dark, towering jak trees silhouette against the night sky. Long exposure, 85mm lens.

Detail shot from inside the bus, looking out through a rain-streaked window. Blurry shapes of dark trees and the red-earth road are visible, reflecting the bus's internal light. The window glass is heavily distorted by rain. A sense of isolation. 100mm macro lens.

scenes.narration: It was then, as Ranga pulled his head back inside, that he saw it. A figure, slumped in the very last row of seats, pressed against the window. It hadn’t been there before, he was sure. Or had it? He’d been busy checking tickets earlier, preoccupied with his new responsibilities. The bus's dim light didn't quite reach that far back, leaving the figure mostly in shadow. It seemed to be facing outwards, towards the deluge beyond the glass, utterly still. Ranga frowned. Another sleepy passenger, he thought, probably got on at the last stop without him noticing amidst the brief flurry. He decided to wait a bit, let the man settle before approaching for his fare. But a tiny, cold tendril of unease had already begun to unfurl in his gut.
visuals: Wide shot from Ranga's perspective, looking towards the back of the bus. A solitary, indistinct figure is slumped in the very last row, pressed against the window, mostly in shadow. The dim overhead lights barely reach this far. Rain streaks the window behind the figure. 35mm film.

Detail shot of the back of an old bus seat, with a dark, crumpled shape of a person's upper back and head visible, turned towards the rain-streaked window. The figure is indistinct, shadowy, blending into the dark upholstery. Only the silhouette is clear. 85mm lens.

scenes.narration: A few minutes passed. Ranga, feeling the chill from the rain-soaked air, decided to collect the fare. He walked down the narrow aisle, the bus swaying gently, rocking him side to side. As he got closer, the figure remained motionless. It wore a dark, crumpled sarong and a faded shirt, its back slightly hunched. Ranga cleared his throat. 'Aiya,' he said softly, 'Ticket, please.' No response. The figure didn't even stir. Ranga reached the last row, standing over it. He could see now the rough texture of the fabric, the faint scent of damp earth and something else, something stale. Still, the head remained turned, facing the streaked window. Soma Aiya caught Ranga's eye in the rearview mirror, a flicker of something unreadable in his gaze.
visuals: Wide shot down the aisle of the bus. Ranga's back as he walks towards the last row. The slumped, indistinct figure is visible in the distance. The bus interior is dimly lit, swaying gently. Rain streaks the windows on both sides. 50mm lens.

Detail shot of the back of the figure's head and hunched shoulders, seen from slightly above and behind, as if Ranga is standing over it. The hair is matted. The face is turned entirely to the window, obscured. Rain streaks heavily outside. 100mm lens.

scenes.narration: Ranga tried again, a little louder this time. 'Aiya, your ticket.' The figure did not move. Not a twitch. It was as if carved from stone, or simply not... present. A profound stillness emanated from it, an almost suffocating sense of sorrow and exhaustion. Ranga felt a coldness that had nothing to do with the night air. He noticed the hair, matted and disheveled, clinging to the back of its neck. The bus hit a pothole, rattling violently, but the figure remained perfectly immobile. Ranga's heart began to thud, a frantic drum against his ribs. This was not a sleeping man. This was something else. He felt an irrational urge to turn and run, to pretend he hadn't seen it at all. He felt a deep, chilling dread.
visuals: Wide shot from Ranga's slightly retreating position, looking towards the indistinct figure at the back of the bus. The shadows around the figure seem to deepen, creating a sense of heavy presence. The bus interior feels colder. 35mm film, slightly desaturated.

Detail shot focusing on the texture of a worn, dark sarong and a faded shirt on a hunched back. The fabric appears damp, clinging. The general sense of sorrowful, heavy atmosphere. 85mm lens, shallow depth of field.

scenes.narration: Ranga slowly backed away, his eyes still fixed on the unmoving form. His breath hitched in his throat. He looked to Soma Aiya in the mirror again, a silent plea for explanation. Soma Aiya's face was grim, his knuckles white on the steering wheel. The driver didn't look back this time, but his voice, low and steady, cut through the rain's din. 'Don't disturb it, putha,' he murmured, almost to himself. 'Just leave it be. Some passengers… they just need to ride.' His tone left no room for question, no room for Ranga's new-found terror. He knew then. This was the one. The uninvited passenger, the legend. And he had almost acknowledged it. The bus seemed to hold its breath as it wound deeper into the mountains.
visuals: Wide shot from Ranga's perspective, looking towards the front of the bus. Soma Aiya's hands are white-knuckled on the steering wheel, his back tense. Ranga's reflection, looking distressed, is barely visible in the rearview mirror. The rain continues outside. 35mm film.

Detail shot of Soma Aiya's hands gripping the steering wheel, knuckles white. The road ahead is blurred by rain and darkness. A hint of a worried expression on his profile, but no direct face shot. 50mm lens.

scenes.narration: Ranga, shaken, retreated to his seat by the door, trying to make himself small. His duty, his pride, warred with a primordial fear he'd never known. He should go back, demand the ticket, it was his job! But Soma Aiya’s words, and the unnatural stillness of the figure, held him captive. He kept glancing back, furtively, through the gaps between the seats. The figure remained, a dark, silent sentinel. The air around it seemed thicker, colder, tinged with an invisible grief. Every bump in the road, every swish of the wipers, amplified the quiet dread. He knew, with a certainty that chilled him to the bone, that he must not speak to it again. He must not acknowledge its presence. Not one more word.
visuals: Wide shot from the front of the bus, looking back. Ranga is in his seat near the door, hunched, constantly glancing back towards the shadowy, indistinct figure at the very end of the aisle. The sense of a heavy, unseen presence. 35mm film.
Detail shot of a dark, empty bus aisle stretching towards the back. The last row remains shrouded in deep shadow, hinting at an unseen presence. Rain streaks heavily on the side windows. 85mm lens.

scenes.narration: Finally, mercifully, the bus pulled into the Badulla bus stand. The rain had eased to a drizzle. The few remaining passengers, yawning and stretching, began to disembark. Ranga, his heart still thumping, tried to act normal, helping them down with their bags. He watched each one carefully, hoping to see the dark figure. But it didn't appear. As the last passenger stepped off, Ranga hesitated. Then, taking a deep breath, he walked quickly to the back of the bus. The seat, where the figure had been, was empty. Utterly empty. Not a stray bag, not a damp patch. Nothing. Yet, the air there felt heavy, like a lingering whisper, a cold echo of something that had been profoundly, sorrowfully present just moments before. He touched the seat, expecting dampness, but it was dry.
visuals: Wide shot of the Badulla bus stand at night, dimly lit by streetlights. The Kandy-Badulla bus is parked, its door open. Passengers disembarking, walking away into the light drizzle. Ranga's back as he looks towards the empty bus interior. 35mm film.

Detail shot of the last row of seats in the bus, now completely empty. The bus interior lights cast long shadows. The seats are dry. Rain outside is a light drizzle, visible through the window. 50mm lens.

scenes.narration: Ranga stumbled back to the front, pale and trembling. Soma Aiya met his gaze in the rearview mirror, a flicker of sad understanding in his eyes. He didn't say 'I told you so,' but the look was enough. The journey back to Kandy was silent, save for the hum of the engine and the distant rumble of thunder. Ranga couldn't shake the image of the silent passenger, or the heavy, sorrowful atmosphere it carried. Every shadow seemed to shift, every reflection in the window seemed to hold a fleeting, indistinct face. He felt watched, even though the bus was now truly empty, heading back up the mountain. The weight of the experience pressed down on him, a cold stone in his chest. He knew he wouldn't forget this night.
visuals: Wide shot from the front of the bus, looking down the now entirely empty aisle on the return journey. The interior is still dimly lit, feeling vast and hollow. Rain has stopped, but the road is wet. Soma Aiya's silhouette in the driver's seat. 35mm film.

Detail shot of the rearview mirror, reflecting a blurred view of the empty bus cabin behind. Soma Aiya's eyes are visible in the mirror, looking towards Ranga's approximate position, a solemn, knowing expression. Shallow depth of field.

scenes.narration: The next morning, back in Kandy, Ranga felt a profound exhaustion. He reached into his money bag to count his earnings from the night's run. It was empty. Completely. He searched frantically, turning the bag inside out, checking every pocket. Nothing. The fare box was correct, but his personal share, his daily wage, was gone. He remembered Soma Aiya’s words: 'ill fortune to anyone who acknowledges its presence.' He hadn't *acknowledged* it, not fully, but he had seen it, tried to speak to it. He had known fear. He never spoke of the incident to anyone again, not truly. But every time he worked the Badulla night bus, a shiver ran down his spine. The roads were long, the night was dark, and some passengers, you just leave them be. If you enjoyed this tale, do hit the like button. It helps us find more stories from the darkest corners of our island.
visuals: Wide shot of a humble, dimly lit room in a Kandy boarding house. Ranga sits on a simple bed, looking distressed, turning his empty money bag inside out. A single kerosene lamp provides warm light. Morning light barely filters through a window. 35mm film.

Detail shot of an empty, worn leather money bag, held open by two hands, showing its complete emptiness. The hands are slightly trembling. A faint, distant sound of temple drums can be heard from outside. 50mm lens.

visuals: Vertical shot from inside a dimly lit bus, looking down the aisle towards a solitary, indistinct figure slumped in the very last row against the rain-streaked window. Shadows dominate. 35mm film.
Vertical shot of the back of a bus seat, with a dark, crumpled shape of a person's upper back and matted head visible, turned entirely to a heavily rain-streaked window. Obscured face. 85mm lens.
Vertical shot from Ranga's eye-level, looking towards the unmoving, silent figure at the back. The air around it seems thick, heavy. Rain blurs the world outside. 50mm lens.
Vertical shot, blurred view of a bus aisle as if Ranga is quickly backing away. The shadowy figure at the end is in focus, appearing more menacing now. 35mm film.
Vertical shot of a bus window, heavily streaked with rain, distorting the dark mountain landscape outside. The interior is dim, reflecting a vague, sorrowful presence. 100mm lens.

shorts.title: VANISHED ON THE BADULLA BUS
shorts.narration: The bus pulled into Badulla, the rain easing. Ranga, the young conductor, helped the last few passengers disembark, his eyes darting, searching. He watched each one carefully, looking for the dark, silent figure he’d seen slumped in the back row. But it didn't appear. As the bus emptied, Ranga, his heart pounding, walked quickly to the very back. The seat, where the figure had been, was empty. Utterly empty. Not a trace, not a damp patch. Yet, the air there felt heavy, like a lingering whisper, a cold echo of something profoundly, sorrowfully present just moments before. He touched the dry seat, a shiver running down his spine. visuals: Vertical shot of an old Kandy-Badulla bus parked at a dimly lit bus stand at night. Its door is open. Passengers are disembarking in a light drizzle. Ranga's silhouette is at the front. 35mm film.
Vertical shot looking down the empty aisle of a bus from the front. The last row of seats is visible, utterly empty, with a lingering sense of coldness. Rain has stopped. 50mm lens.
Vertical shot of a bus seat, previously occupied, now completely empty and dry. The upholstery is worn. The window behind is clear, showing only the dark night. 85mm lens.
Vertical shot of Ranga's trembling hand reaching out to touch an empty bus seat. His face is not visible, only the hand and the seat. 100mm lens.
Vertical shot of a bus interior, lights casting long shadows on the empty seats. The atmosphere is quiet, heavy, as if a profound presence has just departed. 35mm film.
